evidence.claim: CAVA was provided in the candidate chunk as a high-attention, large-cap, reference-lane fast-casual restaurant operator with a hypothesis-level relation to restaurant demand, growth-concept unit economics, new-unit productivity, restaurant margins, throughput, and premium consumer demand.
The candidate chunk identifies the key verification path for CAVA as new-unit AUVs, restaurant margins, traffic versus price, labor productivity, food cost, development cadence, and cohort maturity.
CAVA is better used as a benchmark for smaller restaurant concepts and restaurant-adjacent suppliers than as the primary underfollowed Serenity discovery candidate.
evidence.source_title: Serenity methodology applied to user-provided candidate chunk

memory_update.decision: Keep as reference benchmark, not underfollowed discovery candidate.
memory_update.rationale: High public attention and large-cap status reduce underfollowed discovery value; useful for falsifying restaurant-demand and unit-economics assumptions across smaller operators and adjacent suppliers.

memory_update.task: Use CAVA disclosures as a benchmark against underfollowed candidates in restaurant software, beverage supply, foodservice distribution, equipment, packaging, and store-development infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: New-unit AUVs, restaurant margins, traffic versus price, labor productivity, food cost, development cadence, and cohort maturity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The provided chunk does not include fresh primary filings, segment-level margin evidence, store cohort disclosures, valuation context, or independent confirmation of unit-level bottlenecks. Before promoting beyond reference status, verify current 10-K/10-Q disclosures, comparable restaurant sales, traffic mix, restaurant-level profit margin, food and labor inflation, net new restaurant openings, cash-on-cash returns, and whether any supplier, software, or real-estate bottleneck is actually constraining growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: CAVA is useful as a reference benchmark for high-growth fast-casual restaurant economics: traffic versus price, new-unit productivity, AUV progression, restaurant-level margin, labor productivity, food cost control, cohort maturity, and development cadence. It helps test whether the Restaurants theme is primarily a consumer-demand story or whether value is migrating to less obvious bottlenecks such as supply coordination, food inputs, labor-saving systems, POS/loyalty/order-routing software, and store-development infrastructure.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. The candidate chunk explicitly classifies CAVA as high-attention, large-cap, and reference-lane. It should not receive discovery credit under the Serenity funnel because the hidden-signal path is more likely to be found in smaller suppliers, restaurant software vendors, beverage/input platforms, equipment providers, or distributors rather than in the visible growth restaurant operator itself.

summary: Single-candidate Layer 3 ranking for the Restaurants theme. CAVA is retained only as a high-attention reference model for fast-casual demand, unit economics, throughput, restaurant-level margin, and valuation-pressure benchmarking. It is not an underfollowed chokepoint candidate, and its priority is constrained by weak chunk-level evidence, large-cap attention, and limited supplier-scarcity exposure.
